newsitem.title: UK: Blair vows to take economy decisions for long term.
newsitem.headline: Blair vows to take economy decisions for long term.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Tuesday his government would make economic decisions for the long term, even if they meant short-term unpopularity.
"We have to take the decisions on the economy necessary for the long term," Blair told BBC radio's Jimmy Young Programme.
He gave as an example the three increases in interest rates since the May 1 election -- the last two of them made by the operationally independent Bank of England -- to curb inflation.
The central bank and the Treasury had been advising the outgoing Conservative government for six to nine months to raise interest rates, Blair said.
"It should have been done then. Now, for perfectly understandable political reasons, it wasn't done because they had an election coming up. So we've had to take the action now," he said.
Blair said he was determined to prevent Britain's economy slipping back into bad old habits of boom and bust.
"We mustn't get back into that situation again. If we do that, we will really have a crisis," he said.
